extracted.intended_audience: media researchers, journalists, policymakers, and industry professionals interested in the Finnish news ecosystem
extracted.subtask_description: A country-level profile of Finland's news media environment covering audience metrics, business models, ownership, public service broadcasting, use of AI, journalistic self-regulation, and trust indicators. Intended to summarize current trends and key figures relevant to media policy and industry strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual demographic metric used to interpret scale and reach of news organisations and market dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet penetration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key contextual metric indicating the potential digital reach and maturity of online news consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength of regional press
rubrics_metrics.description: Finland’s news media environment features a strong regional press
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of a strong regional press is treated as an important structural feature of the media ecosystem; relevant for assessing local news provision and resilience when national outlets decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and strength of public service broadcaster (Yle)
rubrics_metrics.description: A strong public service broadcaster (Yle) that is widely seen as trustworthy and important, financed mainly by an annual Yle-tax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates PSB's influence, public trust, funding model (Yle-tax up to €163), and its contested position vis-à-vis commercial media (allegations of unfair competition and ongoing parliamentary review of remit/funding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of national upmarket daily and high-reach tabloids
rubrics_metrics.description: One widely read national upmarket daily (Helsingin Sanomat), and two popular evening tabloids, both reaching over half of the adult population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates market structure and audience segmentation (upmarket national vs mass-market tabloids) important for editorial diversity and commercial strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital transition: reduction in print frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Several regional newspapers moving away from daily print publication; some now appear in print fewer weekdays (example: Kaleva now prints Monday to Saturday).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational/business shift metric showing how news organisations adapt to declining print revenues and delivery costs by reducing print frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declining print revenues and delivery cost pressures
rubrics_metrics.description: Declining print revenues and increasing delivery costs have hit newspapers hard in sparsely populated Finland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business viability criterion explaining drivers behind consolidation, cost-cutting, and changing distribution strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspaper online advertising trend
rubrics_metrics.description: Newspaper online advertising (free city papers included) decreased 1.4% from 2022 to 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific commercial metric used to assess digital revenue health and the limits of ad-funded models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share of payers for online news
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of payers for online news has stayed flat since 2020 and is now 20%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator of willingness to pay and subscription market penetration; used alongside concentration figures to assess sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscriptions are heavily concentrated, with 51% of Finnish respondents with a current digital subscription saying it is to Helsingin Sanomat; 38% pay for regional or local news online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures market concentration among digital subscribers and the relative strength of national vs regional subscription take-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paid sections / metered premium content strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Tabloids introduced paid 'Plus'/'Extra' sections while leaving most site content free; both publish a few paid stories per day and price subscriptions at €6.99/month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Product strategy example demonstrating hybrid free/paid models and specific pricing and adoption (Iltalehti Plus: 18% of subscribers said they had subscribed) as indicators of monetisation approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curation/audio-aggregation business model (Briif)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Finnish startup, Briif, selects newspaper and magazine stories and delivers them in audio for €11.99/month or €99.99/year; media houses are paid proportionally to content listened to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New distribution/curation model metric showing third-party aggregation, targeted audiences (young women), licensing/royalty arrangements, and potential expansion strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media ownership concentration and consolidation
rubrics_metrics.description: Concentration of Finnish regional media into the hands of two main players, Sanoma and Keskisuomalainen, continued via acquisitions; Bonnier became majority owner of Hufvudstadsbladet and two local newspapers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structural criterion highlighting consolidation, cross-ownership, philanthropic ownership transitions (Konstsamfundet), and implications for plurality and local news provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of artificial intelligence in newsrooms
rubrics_metrics.description: Finnish major news companies are actively adopting artificial intelligence tools and have set up special teams; generative AI already helps compose headlines, shorten stories, or write summaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational/process criterion indicating changing newsroom workflows and technology adoption; relevant for quality control, editorial practices, and innovation assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalistic Guidelines update on sponsored content
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated Journalistic Guidelines (accepted April 2024; effective October) state that sponsored articles are allowed but the funder must be clearly stated if they affect the choice of subject area; all other decisions about journalistic content must be made independently of the funder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical/self-regulatory standard specifying disclosure requirements and editorial independence rules for sponsored content; includes timing of adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust in news (survey metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in news overall: 69%; Finnish news remains among the most highly trusted among surveyed countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience trust indicator used to evaluate perceived credibility of the media system; contextual note that Finnish media are not politically polarised and scepticism tends to target tabloids or outlets with tabloid image.

rubrics_metrics.name: RSF World Press Freedom Index score
rubrics_metrics.description: RSF World Press Freedom Index: 5/180, Score 86.55.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International press freedom ranking used as a comparative indicator of the legal and practical environment for journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience behaviour metrics (news use and podcast listening)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of online news sources is almost 90% weekly reach; television news and the printed press continue slow decline; 34% listened to a podcast in the last month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumption metrics describing audience habits and platform shifts relevant for editorial planning and distribution strategies.
